description: FIND-002 (sprint-5) is RESOLVED for the literal records[-1] regression, but the static fence is regex-narrow. The records[-1] regression is fenced ONLY by the static check `absent "records\[-1\]"` (test-akt-treasury.sh:22), NOT by the behavioral run: the impl never calls `bme ledger`, so the new fake ledger branch (test-akt-treasury.sh:35 returning records[-1]=canceled) is dead at runtime in every executed/canceled run — it is inert decoration. The static check greps the comment-stripped source (src via `sed 's/#.*//'`, test-akt-treasury.sh:11), which correctly tolerates the two legitimate `records[-1]` mentions in the impl COMMENTS (akt-treasury.sh:62-63) while rejecting any executable `records[-1]`. However the regex `records\[-1\]` would NOT catch a semantically-equivalent stale-ledger regression written as `.records | last` or `.records[-1:]` or `last(.records[])` (jq idioms) — those read the same last record without the literal `[-1]` token. The manifest's named regression (literal records[-1]) is caught; near-equivalent rewrites are not. This is non-blocking because the literal form is the one the live-run trap and the impl comment reference, but the fake's ledger branch gives a FALSE impression of behavioral coverage it does not provide.

evidence.snippet:
absent "records\[-1\]"  ... (static, comment-stripped src)
*"query bme ledger"*) echo '{"records":[{"status":"...canceled"}]}'  # dead: impl never calls bme ledger
